title: bug: GraphQL API rate limits not gracefully handled for power users
body:
### Description

Users fetching a massive set of badges or contribution graphs occasionally hit GitHub’s API rate limiting, resulting in silent failures or incomplete graphs.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Batch load multiple user profiles with deep (~1000+) histories simultaneously
2. Monitor for partial data loads or rate limit errors in console

### Expected Behavior

API rate limiting should be detected and communicated to the user, ideally with a retry or backoff mechanism.

### Screenshots / Logs

_No response_

### GitHub Username (If applicable)

_No response_

### Environment

Chrome

title: feat: Deep GraphQL caching and smart sync strategies
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

GraphQL API syncs all data on every update, resulting in redundant traffic and slower UX for large datasets.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Implement smart caching/invalidation strategies client and server side for GraphQL contribution data, with delta sync and partial update support.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Manual cache refreshes or short polling intervals, which remain inefficient.

title: feat: Advanced 3D isometric customization options
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Current 3D isometric monoliths offer limited real-time customization and lack advanced interactive controls for geometry and perspective.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Add support for customizing and animating 3D monolith tilt/rotation, light direction, and real-time perspective controls in the web UI.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Preset themes with fixed 3D angles or offering only basic perspective tools.

title: Enhance the /claim Bot Welcome Message
body:
## 📝 Description

When a contributor comments `/claim` on an issue, our custom GitHub Action (`.github/scripts/issue-management/claim-handler.js`) assigns them to it. Currently, it likely just assigns the user without much feedback. 

To improve the open-source contributor experience for GSSoC, the bot should reply with a friendly, detailed comment explaining the rules (e.g., the 3-day expiry limit).

## ✅ Tasks

- [ ] Open `.github/scripts/issue-management/claim-handler.js`.
- [ ] After successfully calling the GitHub API to assign the user, use `github.rest.issues.createComment` to post a reply.
- [ ] The reply should look something like this:
  ```markdown
  🎉 **Assigned!** Welcome to the project, @{username}. 
  
  ⏳ **Reminder:** You have **3 days** to submit a Pull Request. After 3 days of inactivity, you will be automatically unassigned to give others a chance (as per our GSSoC anti-hoarding policy).
  
  Happy coding! 🚀

   ```

## 📁 Files to Touch

    .github/scripts/issue-management/claim-handler.js
